1	# tomlctl
2	
3	Small TOML read/write CLI for Claude Code flow and ledger files.
4	
5	Built because `python3 -c "import tomllib"` is unreliable on Windows Git Bash, and the canonical flow/ledger schemas (`.claude/flows/*/context.toml`, `review-ledger.toml`, `optimise-findings.toml`) require parse-rewrite operations rather than line-level edits.
6	
7	## Install
8	
9	```bash
10	cargo install --path .
11	```
12	
13	Requires Rust 1.85+.
14	
15	## Usage
16	
17	See [`claude/skills/tomlctl/SKILL.md`](../claude/skills/tomlctl/SKILL.md) for the full reference.
18	
19	Quick tour:
20	
21	```bash
22	tomlctl get         <file> [path]                     # JSON of value (or whole file)
23	tomlctl set         <file> <path> <value> [--type T]  # scalar
24	tomlctl set-json    <file> <path> --json <json>       # array / object / scalar
25	tomlctl validate    <file>                            # parse-check
26	tomlctl items list  <file> [--status X] [--category Y] [--newer-than YYYY-MM-DD] [--file PATH] [--count]
27	tomlctl items get   <file> <id>
28	tomlctl items add   <file> --json '{"id":"R7",...}'
29	tomlctl items update <file> <id> --json '{"status":"fixed"}' [--unset key]...
30	tomlctl items remove <file> <id>
31	tomlctl items next-id <file> [--prefix R|O]
32	tomlctl items apply  <file> --ops '[{"op":"add|update|remove", ...}, ...]' [--array NAME]
33	tomlctl items find-duplicates <file> [--tier A|B|C]    # dedup hygiene, read-only JSON array
34	tomlctl items orphans  <file>                          # missing-file / symbol-missing / dangling-dep
35	tomlctl blocks verify  <file>... [--block <marker-name>]...  # cross-file shared-block parity
36	
37	# Global flags (accepted before or after the subcommand):
38	#   --allow-outside           bypass the best-effort .claude/ containment guard (not a sandbox)
39	#   --no-write-integrity      suppress the <file>.sha256 sidecar on write
40	#   --verify-integrity        verify <file> against <file>.sha256 before any read
41	```
42	
43	Every `--ops` and `--json` flag also accepts `-` as a sentinel to read the JSON payload from stdin — use this for large batches or payloads containing shell metacharacters:
44	
45	```bash
46	printf '%s' "$ops_json" | tomlctl items apply <file> --ops -
47	
48	tomlctl items apply <file> --ops - <<'EOF'
49	[{"op":"update","id":"R1","json":{"status":"fixed"}}]
50	EOF
51	```
52	
53	All commands print JSON on stdout, exit non-zero on failure.
54	
55	## Design
56	
57	- Uses [`toml 1.1.2+spec-1.1.0`](https://crates.io/crates/toml) with `preserve_order` for stable key layout.
58	- Whole-file parse → mutate → re-serialise. No format preservation (flow/ledger schemas forbid inline comments).
59	- Dates round-trip as TOML date literals; JSON strings matching `YYYY-MM-DD` are promoted to dates on write.
60	- **Integrity sidecar.** Every write emits `<file>.sha256` alongside the target, in standard `sha256sum` format (`<64-hex>  <basename>\n`), written atomically after the primary rename so an interleaved reader cannot see a torn pair. Pass `--no-write-integrity` to opt out. Pass `--verify-integrity` on any invocation to verify the target against its sidecar before every read — a missing sidecar or digest mismatch aborts with expected/actual hashes named in the error. `tomlctl` never auto-repairs; a mismatch means either an out-of-band edit or a corrupted sidecar, and a human should decide which. **Threat model.** The sidecar is a consistency check against accidental corruption and collaborative out-of-band edits — it is **not** a MAC or tamper-proof signature. An attacker with ledger write access can trivially rewrite the sidecar; hostile-actor threat models still require auditing the ledger's git history.
61

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	set -euo pipefail
3	
4	cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)"
5	
6	MANIFEST="${MANIFEST:-scripts/shared-blocks.toml}"
7	
8	if [[ ! -f $MANIFEST ]]; then
9	  echo "error: manifest not found at $MANIFEST" >&2
10	  exit 2
11	fi
12	
13	if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
14	  HASHER='sha256sum'
15	elif command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
16	  HASHER='shasum -a 256'
17	else
18	  echo "error: need sha256sum or shasum -a 256 on PATH" >&2
19	  exit 2
20	fi
21	
22	hash_block() {
23	  local file=$1 name=$2
24	  awk -v start="<!-- SHARED-BLOCK:${name} START -->" \
25	      -v end="<!-- SHARED-BLOCK:${name} END -->" '
26	    $0 == start { in_block=1; next }
27	    $0 == end   { in_block=0; next }
28	    in_block    { print }
29	  ' "$file" | $HASHER | awk '{print $1}'
30	}
31	
32	pairs=$(awk '
33	  /^\[\[block\]\]/ { name=""; in_files=0; next }
34	  /^name = "/ {
35	    gsub(/^name = "|"$/, "")
36	    name=$0
37	    next
38	  }
39	  /^files = \[/ { in_files=1; next }
40	  in_files && /^\]/ { in_files=0; name=""; next }
41	  in_files && /^[[:space:]]*"[^"]+"/ {
42	    gsub(/^[[:space:]]*"|",?$|"$/, "")
43	    if (name != "") print name "\t" $0
44	  }
45	' "$MANIFEST")
46	
47	if [[ -z $pairs ]]; then
48	  echo "error: manifest yielded no (block, file) pairs — check $MANIFEST syntax" >&2
49	  exit 2
50	fi
51	
52	fail=0
53	declare -A first_hash first_file
54	
55	while IFS=$'\t' read -r bname bfile; do
56	  [[ -z $bname || -z $bfile ]] && continue
57	
58	  if [[ ! -f $bfile ]]; then
59	    echo "error: block '$bname' references missing file: $bfile" >&2
60	    fail=1
61	    continue
62	  fi
63	
64	  if ! grep -qF "<!-- SHARED-BLOCK:${bname} START -->" "$bfile"; then
65	    echo "error: $bfile missing START marker for block '$bname'" >&2
66	    fail=1
67	    continue
68	  fi
69	  if ! grep -qF "<!-- SHARED-BLOCK:${bname} END -->" "$bfile"; then
70	    echo "error: $bfile missing END marker for block '$bname'" >&2
71	    fail=1
72	    continue
73	  fi
74	
75	  h=$(hash_block "$bfile" "$bname")
76	
77	  if [[ -z ${first_hash[$bname]:-} ]]; then
78	    first_hash[$bname]=$h
79	    first_file[$bname]=$bfile
80	  elif [[ ${first_hash[$bname]} != "$h" ]]; then
81	    echo "error: block '$bname' drift:" >&2
82	    printf '  %s  hash=%s\n' "${first_file[$bname]}" "${first_hash[$bname]}" >&2
83	    printf '  %s  hash=%s\n' "$bfile" "$h" >&2
84	    fail=1
85	  fi
86	done <<< "$pairs"
87	
88	if [[ $fail -eq 0 ]]; then
89	  echo "shared-block parity: OK"
90	fi
91	exit $fail
